questions.question: After the second F1 launches the browser, what happens to the help panel?

options.label: Close it
options.description: The panel dismisses and you're back at the TUI. You asked for the browser; the panel has done its job. Matches how every other key already dismisses the overlay.

options.label: Leave it open
options.description: The panel stays up. Lets you press F1 repeatedly, and keeps the keybindings visible while you read GitHub in another window. Risk: no visible feedback that anything happened, since the browser opens behind the terminal.

questions.question: The panel currently ends with "Esc / q to close". A second F1 is invisible unless we say so. Should the panel advertise it?

options.label: Add a hint line
options.description: e.g. "F1 again to open the FlightDeck repo on GitHub" in the footer next to the close hint. Undiscoverable otherwise — nobody presses a key twice on a hunch.

options.label: Hint plus a Global entry
options.description: Footer hint, and add "F1 — Help / keybindings" to the Global shortcuts section so F1 shows up in its own list alongside the existing "?" entry.

options.label: No hint
options.description: Keep the panel exactly as it is. Hidden gesture for people who happen to try it.

questions.question: If the browser can't be launched (no xdg-open handler, spawn fails), what should the user see?

options.label: Error notification overlay
options.description: Replace the help panel with the existing notification dialog carrying the error text — the same path file_manager failures already take. Honest and consistent.

options.label: Silent
options.description: Swallow it. Nothing happens, no message. Least code, but the user is left guessing whether F1 did anything at all.
